extracted.intended_audience: software teams, engineers, designers, and product managers evaluating MacOS collaboration tools
extracted.subtask_description: A product landing page describing features, capabilities, and benefits of a MacOS-first multiplayer collaboration app (Multi). Focuses on real‑time screensharing, shared control, AI summaries, and integrations for software teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplayer by default
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplayer by default — Communicate faster with shared cursors & drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that collaboration is the default mode (not an opt-in); shared cursors and drawing are highlighted as primary communication affordances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous screensharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Work across screenshares from up to 10 people—at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports multiple concurrent screenshares so many participants can present or interact simultaneously; presented as a scalability and workflow benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyboard-first workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Keyboard-first — Stay in flow with commands & customizable shortcuts. Or use the Raycast extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritizes keyboard commands and shortcuts (and third‑party extension support) to minimize context switching and keep users 'in flow'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared control with low latency
rubrics_metrics.description: Shared control — Lend a helping hand by clicking & typing into anyone's apps, with sub-100ms latency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real‑time remote control (clicking and typing into others' apps) is a core feature, with a specific latency target (sub‑100ms) used as a quality metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic deep links / magic links
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic deep links — Open designs, code, or docs, without waiting for someone to share the link. Skip sending links to designs or files, with automatic magic links to screenshares locally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminates manual link sharing by creating local deep links to resources featured in a session; presented as reducing friction in finding referenced files.

rubrics_metrics.name: World-class audio/video quality
rubrics_metrics.description: World-class audio/video quality — Built on Zoom’s world-class infra, plus custom upgrades for crispness and latency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims enterprise-grade A/V quality by leveraging Zoom infrastructure plus proprietary improvements; quality and latency are explicit selling points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sessions that document themselves / post-async
rubrics_metrics.description: Sessions that document themselves — Post async, then cancel that update meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positioning that meetings/sessions generate artifacts (summaries, logs) reducing the need for follow-up update meetings; implies documentation and asynchronous sharing are built-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI summaries (accurate & concise)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI summaries — Save time with summaries that are accurate and concise enough to post in Slack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries are marketed for accuracy and concision to be shareable directly to team communication channels; suggests an expectation of reliability for downstream use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic capture of action items
rubrics_metrics.description: Action items — Automatically capture action items, then generate Linear Issues with 1 click.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated extraction of action items and one‑click integration with issue trackers (Linear) is a productivity feature and an interoperability standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference log / session history
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference log — Get straight back to any file or link that was screenshared or sent in chat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains an index of resources used in sessions so participants can quickly return to referenced files or links; pitched as reducing friction after meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive Q&A / custom prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask questions — Go deeper or quickly draft follow ups with custom prompts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides in‑session interactive questioning and prompt-driven drafting to accelerate follow-ups and deeper exploration without leaving the session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording for onboarding and details
rubrics_metrics.description: Recording — Capture all the details for your next onboarding with recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records sessions to preserve details for tasks like onboarding; positioned as a knowledge-capture and reuse capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy defaults and user control
rubrics_metrics.description: Privacy defaults — Summarize by default, or only when you need it. You’re in control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights configurable privacy/summarization defaults so users can choose when automated features (like summaries) run, indicating attention to user consent and control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrations and platform reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Push Action Items to Linear; Raycast extension; iOS Beta; Images in Chat; Better Detail in Summaries, Questions & Drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changelog items and featured integrations show ongoing product development and interoperability (issue tracker integration, extensions, mobile support, richer chat/media), which serve as practical criteria for evaluating platform maturity.
